A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DecompDreamer. Their main texts, equations, algorithms, tables, figures and appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial retitling and reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original generated scenes, component ablations, quantitative comparisons on 30 prompts and a 20-participant user study.

after.justification: V2 reports original generation comparisons and ablations, plus loss trajectories, runtime comparisons, additional alignment scores and illustrated failure cases.

M1.justification: V2 adds a separate translation-only pre-optimization loop with other object parameters frozen (Section 5.2.3, Algorithm 1); v1 applies translations within the main optimization loop. The core two-stage schedule, VLM/Point-E initialization and SD3.5 backbone remain. Inconsistent FMD-to-SDS terminology does not establish a further procedural change.

E1.justification: Both retain evaluation on 30 compositional prompts spanning 2–11 objects. V2 additionally tests fine-grained human-part decomposition and a partially open backpack containing a teddy bear (Figure 14), extending the tested task requirements beyond the original distinct-object compositions.

E2.justification: Trellis is newly evaluated, replacing HiFA in Table 1 and Magic3D in Figure 4. HiFA and Magic3D remain in appendix comparisons. Most existing comparators are retained.

E3.justification: V2 substantially expands evaluation through a grounding-based Text-to-3D Alignment metric, separate scores for at most three versus more than three objects, loss tracking on a four-object prompt, and runtime comparisons across five object counts. The reported 30-prompt, 20-participant study size remains unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds convergence analysis using object, relationship and scene losses (Figure 5), quantitative complexity and runtime analyses, and explicit failure cases (Figure 14). These probe optimization behavior, scalability and applicability boundaries. Most original schedule, azimuth, negative-prompt, translation and backbone ablations are retained or relocated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for the comparisons. V2's additional averages and object-count breakdowns do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes reported overall Pick-A-Pic from 22.5 to 24.0 and user preference from 54 to 61 for DecompDreamer, while CLIP remains 34.5. V2 adds alignment scores, including 73.4 overall, subgroup results, runtime values and loss trajectories. Because comparator membership changes, the preference increase is not an established same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: V2 removes v1 Section 4.1's explicit rectified-flow interpolation and FMD gradient definition, while adding scene-configuration definitions, heuristic objective formulations and a spatial-correction objective. The new Theoretical Foundations section is primarily conceptual and supplies no formal complexity or convergence proof.

C1.justification: V1 presents decomposition, progressive optimization, novel FMD and view-aware disentanglement as its contributions. V2 redefines the central contribution as an implicit curriculum addressing a fundamental gradient-conflict bottleneck, with stronger claims about stable, scalable convergence. FMD is no longer claimed as a distinct novel contribution.

C2.justification: V2 attributes baseline failures to conflicting gradients and optimization schedules, substantially revising v1's explanations centered on representation and relationship modeling. It also adds discussion of viewpoint-sensitive metric weaknesses and complex-action failures, and develops the already acknowledged Janus and fine-grained decomposition limitations with causal explanations and proposed remedies.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents randomized, anonymized video presentation and evaluator instructions, and adds comparative runtimes. It omits v1's guidance scale of 7.5, initialization with 80K points per object and project-page link, although other appendix hyperparameters remain. These disclosure changes do not establish corresponding changes in experimental settings.

R1.justification: V2 adds curriculum-learning, multitask-learning and gradient-surgery literature, alongside Trellis, Eval3D and DreamHOI references. It reorganizes prior methods into optimization heuristics and removes the dedicated rectified-flow discussion, substantially shifting novelty positioning toward scheduling and gradient conflict.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work and conclusion are extensively rewritten around a composition-aware curriculum. V2 inserts a Theoretical Foundations section, condenses and reorganizes the method, and restructures the appendix. This exceeds localized wording changes.

P2.justification: V2 changes from two-column to single-column presentation, adds taxonomy and loss-trajectory figures, a failure-case panel and a runtime table, and expands Table 1 into metric and object-count groups. Existing qualitative and ablation panels are extensively rearranged, resized or relocated.

improvement.justification: The added alignment metric, complexity breakdown, runtime comparisons and failure cases make evaluation more informative. However, v2 removes the explicit FMD formulation and previously reported settings, introduces contradictory SDS descriptions, and asserts gradient-conflict avoidance from loss curves without directly measuring conflict. These material gains in empirical scrutiny and losses in reproducibility and claim support prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
